topic: Agent CodeMode: Let Coding Agent Scripts Call Your Connected MCP Servers
summary: agent-codemode (janwilmake/agent-codemode, MIT, npm agent-codemode@0.1.1) is a small Node 18+ CLI + TypeScript library that lets the scripts your coding agent writes call the MCP servers that agent is *already* logged into. Instead of routing every call through the model, it reads the credentials your coding agent already minted (Claude Code's macOS Keychain item 'Claude Code-credentials' -> mcpOAuth map, or ~/.claude.json / .mcp.json config for stdio and API-key servers; on Linux/Windows from ~/.claude/.credentials.json) and speaks Streamable HTTP MCP or stdio JSON-RPC directly. The pitch rests on one measured number: the author's real prompt (fetch every In Progress Linear ticket with full body and count occurrences of 'mcp' across 39 tickets) consumed 262,159 chars / ~65,500 tokens over 40 sequential tool calls versus 903 chars / ~226 tokens in one script — 290x less into context, 99.66% saved, plus an exact answer instead of an approximate one. It also ships a Claude skill (.claude/skills/agent-codemode/SKILL.md) because the library only matters if the agent knows to reach for it. The honest framing is that almost nothing here is new — code mode was named by Kenton Varda and Sunil Pai at Cloudflare in Sept 2025, Cloudflare's Code Mode puts 2,500 API endpoints behind search()+execute() in ~1,000 tokens, Anthropic ships Programmatic Tool Calling inside the API, and MCPorter already imports server definitions from six editors and has ~5,039 stars / ~538k weekly npm downloads. What is new is a narrow last mile: zero credential setup, because the token is already on the machine. That narrowness is also the security story — the SECURITY.md is candid that any process a Claude Code session can spawn can already read every MCP OAuth token, so the package is an honest demonstration of an existing blast radius rather than a new hole. Adoption is tiny (30 stars, 0 forks, 1 open issue that is a directory invite, ~10 npm downloads/week), the repo has been untouched since 2026-08-19 and has no GitHub releases, and Linux/Windows are best-effort and unverified. Verdict for readers: read it as a 30-line idea worth copying into your own harness and as the clearest write-up of the credential last mile — not as a dependency to adopt.

competitors.name: janwilmake/agent-codemode (the subject)
key_points: MIT, Node >=18, TypeScript; repo created 2026-08-18T10:08:24Z, last push 2026-08-19T07:14:18Z; 30 stars, 0 forks, 1 open issue (issue #1, 2026-09-22, a 'share on GithubStarMate' invite); 33 files tracked, 681 KB; only 2 commits-worth of published versions and no GitHub releases at all.

The claim is deliberately self-limiting: 'Be clear about what is and isn't new here.' Multi-server scripts, typed clients and reading other editors' MCP config are all credited as prior art (Cloudflare sandbox bindings, VoidMCP, mcp-use, LangChain MultiServerMCPClient, MCPorter). The one differing row in its own comparison table is Credentials: 'your agent's, inherited' vs everyone else's API keys or own vault.

Cost evidence is one real prompt, not a benchmark suite: 39-ticket Linear workspace, 262,159 chars (~65,500 tokens) over 40 sequential tool calls vs 903 chars (~226 tokens) in 1 script -> 290x less into context / 99.66% saved. Author labels the token figure as a 4-chars-per-token heuristic and says the ratio, not the absolute, is the durable part.

Two surfaces: CLI (`agent-codemode`, alias `codemode`) subcommands servers / tools / call / types, and a TS API (`mcp` proxy, callTool, listTools, resultText, McpClient.fromClaudeCode). Exit codes 0 ok, 1 credential/transport/usage error, 2 tool reported isError.

`types --all` reads each server's live tools/list and emits a typed .ts module per server plus an index barrel; generated modules declaration-merge into an McpServers interface so a side-effect import is the whole setup and wrong keys/types are compile errors (no cast at the call site).

Verified matrix in README: remote HTTP MCP (OAuth, Keychain) works; self-hosted remote MCP works; plugin MCP (plugin:slack:slack) works; API-key HTTP/SSE via config headers works; stdio via config env works; claude.ai connectors (Gmail, Calendar) explicitly NOT supported.

claude.ai connectors are refused for two stated reasons: the token exists only in claude.ai's backend (absent locally) and the connector endpoint rejects any request whose clientInfo.name contains 'claude' — working around either would be impersonating Claude Code.

It reads other clients' configs too (Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini CLI share the same mcpServers schema), so it inherits every client's stdio and API-key servers; OAuth inheritance is Claude-only for now and other clients' OAuth servers report as 'unsupported'.

Known operational wrinkle: Claude Code rotates refresh tokens single-use (referencing anthropics/claude-code issue #59460), so a stale script-held token can be rejected — the documented fix is to start Claude Code or run `claude mcp login <server>`.

Ships a Claude skill at .claude/skills/agent-codemode/SKILL.md whose argument is behavioural, not technical: an agent that knows the option exists writes one script; an agent that doesn't keeps making twenty tool calls. Docs are explicit that the skill, not the library, is the mechanism behind the token ratio.

Maintenance reality to state plainly: repo untouched since 2026-08-19, no releases endpoint data, ~10 npm downloads in the week of 2026-09-23..29, 0 forks, and the only open issue is a promotional invite. Single maintainer (janwilmake, 259 followers, 368 public repos, 'Independent Researcher & Product Engineer').

competitors.name: Cloudflare Code Mode (the origin of the pattern)
key_points: Kenton Varda and Sunil Pai, September 2025: 'It turns out we've all been using MCP wrong.' The thesis in one line, quoted by every later implementation including agent-codemode: LLMs are better at writing code to call MCP, than at calling MCP directly.

Two stated reasons: (1) agents handle many more and more complex tools when they are presented as a TypeScript API than as direct tool schemas — plausibly because training data is full of real TypeScript and thin on contrived tool-call examples; (2) the pattern shines when calls chain, because with direct tool calls every intermediate output must feed into the model just to be copied into the next call.

Security framing that contrasts with agent-codemode: MCP bindings hide API keys because the binding is an already-authorized client interface and the agent supervisor holds the tokens and injects them — 'the AI cannot possibly write code that leaks any keys'. agent-codemode instead puts the real token in the sandbox that is your shell.
This is the piece agent-codemode explicitly credits as naming the pattern; the README's 'Prior art' section links it rather than claiming invention.

competitors.name: Cloudflare Code Mode MCP server: an entire API in 1,000 tokens
key_points: Server-side application of the same idea: the Cloudflare API has over 2,500 endpoints and exposing each as an MCP tool would consume over 2 million tokens; Code Mode collapses it to two tools — search() and execute() — in roughly 1,000 tokens of context.

Mechanism is discovery-by-code: the model writes JavaScript against a typed representation of the OpenAPI spec, filtering endpoints by product, path or tags; the full spec never enters the model context.

@cloudflare/codemode is actively maintained (cloudflare/agents monorepo: 5,699 stars, last push 2026-09-30) and does ~625,217 npm downloads/week (2026-09-23..29) — three orders of magnitude more distribution than agent-codemode.

The runtime surface is far richer than a CLI: connectors, sandbox executor, search/describe, approve/reject/rollback for paused executions, execution audit records, saved snippets, plus entry points for AI SDK, MCP, TanStack AI, browser iframe executor and a Vite plugin.

competitors.name: Anthropic: Code execution with MCP
key_points: Names the two compounding cost drivers agent-codemode later quantifies on its own data: tool definitions loaded upfront into context, and intermediate tool results passed through the model — a 2-hour sales transcript flowing through twice is called out as ~50,000 extra tokens.

The canonical worked example is the same shape as agent-codemode's Linear demo (gdrive.getDocument -> salesforce.updateRecord, transcript copied twice): the model is used as a data bus, and larger documents break the context window entirely.

Anthropic's own caveat, which any review must repeat: code execution requires a secure execution environment with sandboxing, resource limits and monitoring — infrastructure overhead and security considerations that direct tool calls avoid.

competitors.name: Anthropic: Programmatic Tool Calling (advanced tool use)
key_points: The same pattern shipped inside the Claude Developer Platform API: the model writes Python in Anthropic's sandbox, the code calls the tools, and only the final result returns to context.

Stated benefit over the direct path: 37% fewer tokens on their research tasks with a small accuracy gain on top — a vendor-measured number, useful as a sanity check against the 99.66% single-task figure agent-codemode quotes.
Acknowledgements credit Cloudflare's Code Mode, LLMVM, and 'Code Execution as MCP' as inspirations — the vendor itself does not claim to have invented code mode, and neither should a review.

competitors.name: MCPorter (the closest neighbour, and the honest benchmark)
key_points: 5,039 stars, 347 forks, MIT; created 2025-11-05, last push 2026-10-01T05:42Z (actively maintained daily); ~538,183 npm downloads in the week of 2026-09-23..29 — roughly 54,000x agent-codemode's ~10.

Does everything agent-codemode does and then more: zero-config discovery across Cursor/Claude/Codex/Windsurf/OpenCode/VS Code, `emit-ts` typed clients, `generate-cli` to mint a standalone CLI per server, `serve` as an MCP bridge that aggregates daemons into one server, auto-OAuth for hosted MCPs, transport pooling, and stable --json envelopes.

The single difference agent-codemode claims: MCPorter imports server *definitions* but keeps its own credential vault at ~/.mcporter/credentials.json and makes you run `mcporter auth` per server, whereas agent-codemode reads the token the agent already minted and needs no auth step. That is a narrow difference and the README says so.
Note the naming trap for the writer: the repo now lives at openclaw/mcporter (github.com/openclaw/mcporter, site mcporter.sh); older links to steipete/mcporter redirect.

competitors.name: datalayer/agent-codemode (name collision — different project entirely)
key_points: Same name, unrelated approach: BSD-3-Clause Python package that generates typed *Python* bindings from MCP servers, lets the agent write code that composes tools in a sandbox (eval/monty/docker/jupyter/colab/kaggle/modal variants), and can re-export the generated tools as an MCP server.
Created 2025-11-15, 4 stars, 2 forks, last push 2026-09-26, homepage agent-codemode.datalayer.tech. Much smaller, but maintained longer and with a real (if tiny) user base.

Disambiguation is mandatory in the article body: readers searching 'agent codemode' will land on three different things (this Python package, the janwilmake JS package, and Cloudflare's @cloudflare/codemode), and only one of them is the subject.

competitors.name: @utcp/code-mode (UTCP plug-and-play library)
key_points: 1,578 stars, 108 forks, MPL-2.0; created 2025-11-11, last push 2026-08-25. Agents write TypeScript executed in an isolated VM sandbox with multi-protocol orchestration across MCP, HTTP, File and CLI sources; full console log capture and execution timeouts.

Configuration-first: you maintain a .utcp_config.json listing providers, and wire the code-mode MCP server into Claude Desktop via UTCP_CONFIG_FILE. npm distribution is modest: ~1,051 downloads in the week measured.
Represents the 'sandboxed code mode as a product' branch of the family tree, as opposed to agent-codemode's 'no sandbox, just your shell' branch.

competitors.name: @tmustier/code-mode-mcp benchmark (the evidence every review should cite)
key_points: The most rigorous public benchmark found in this space: @tmustier/code-mode-mcp@0.3.0 with claude-opus-4-8:xhigh, a deterministic 10-tool MCP server, 8 task shapes x 4 conditions x 5 runs = 160 scored runs, every run returning the exact expected answer.

Core finding: there is NO universal call-count threshold. Six independent small lookups favoured direct tools; an 8-step dependent cursor chain and a 19-call list-and-fan-out stage favoured Code Mode. Recommendation is per-stage routing, not a global mode switch.

Hard numbers worth quoting: T3 fetched 4 datasets concurrently and direct MCP returned ~148,000 characters of raw records to the model where Code Mode returned ~100 characters; T4 took 8 model/tool cycles direct vs one exec cell; T5 aggregated 18 result blocks inside one cell.
Hybrid cost is real and must be reported: guided hybrid median initial context 4,328 tokens vs direct-only 3,261 and Code-Mode-only 2,484 — the discovery/guidance surface is not free.

Unguided hybrids made avoidable mistakes (guessed nested tool names, wrong parsing of result.content[0].text) and needed route changes; guidance removed those failures. This is the direct counter-argument to agent-codemode's 'just ship a skill and behaviour changes by default'.

Note the lineage: the repo is now archived in spirit — its description reads 'Deprecated: use nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter's mcpScript' — 1 star, last push 2026-07-16. Cite it as a benchmark, not as a tool recommendation.

competitors.name: Agent Swarm: 26 tool calls, one script, $0.02 (production measurement)
key_points: The cleanest end-to-end production measurement of code mode found: a live workflow-triage run (script id da3b5c7b-b9a6-4f9e-be9e-f682aca48ea0, measured 2026-07-07) put ~6,450 tokens into the model for the script path against a modeled ~815,000 for the raw tool-call path — ~99.2% fewer tokens for that data-gathering step.

Crucially, the same post reports the smaller end-to-end effect honestly: the scheduled task as a whole costs roughly half and runs in 1-2 minutes instead of ~5, because the agent still has to reason about the summary and decide escalations. A review that only quotes 99.2% is misleading.

Operational rule they publish, worth stealing for the article's 'when not to' section: use a script when a job means 10+ similar tool calls, a bulk fan-out, or heavy intermediate data you would otherwise discard; stay with direct tool calls for a handful of calls or when intermediate values must be in context.

Scale claimed as of late July 2026: ~150 reusable scripts, ~25,000 executions in 30 days, ~70% of schedules using at least one — evidence that the pattern compounds once scripts are files rather than one-off calls.

competitors.name: Bifrost / Maxim AI: code mode across 508 tools and 16 MCP servers
key_points: Controlled benchmark: classic MCP consumed 75.1M input tokens where code mode consumed 5.4M for the same query set — 92.8% reduction, with both configurations passing 65 of 65 test queries.

Mechanism at gateway level: four generic meta-tools (listToolFiles, readToolFile, getToolDocs, executeToolCode) replace a 500+ tool catalog; the model sees four tools whether 5 or 50 servers are connected. Enabled per MCP client, so heavy servers run in code mode while small utilities stay direct.

Useful for the article's scaling argument: MCP token cost scales with catalog size, not with work done — a six-turn workflow across 100 tools pays the full definition cost six times before producing a three-line answer.

competitors.name: The official MCP registry, by the numbers (ecosystem context)
key_points: 30,375 unique servers in the official MCP registry as of 2026-09-10 (99,114 server-and-version records), roughly 3x the ~9,650 it held in May 2026; August 2026 alone added more than the registry's entire first five months.
98.9% marked active, 1.1% (332) deprecated, zero visibly deleted — the registry adds, it does not prune.

Publication is top-heavy: top 10 publishers hold 17.7% of all servers, top 50 hold 24.6%, and 16,356 publishers have exactly one server. The largest single publisher has 1,505 servers (arithmetic micro-tools), so raw server counts are inflated by automated publishing.

Transport has flipped to remote: 54.8% of servers are remote-only, 38.9% local-only, 4.9% both; 17,584 remote endpoints use streamable-http vs 1,073 on deprecated sse — which is exactly the transport agent-codemode speaks.

Governance gap to cite: the registry records no auth method, no security review and no uptime check, and ~62% of servers have only one version with ~36% untouched for 3+ months. This is the backdrop for the credential-blast-radius discussion.

competitors.name: MCPorter docs (what a mature version of this looks like)
key_points: Documents itself as leaning into 'the code-execution-with-MCP pattern Anthropic recommends: skip the giant tool-schema prompt, generate a small typed surface, and let the agent or the human call MCP servers like normal functions' — same thesis, productized.

Concrete capability list to contrast against agent-codemode's four CLI verbs: list with --schema, call with colon flags or function-call syntax, resource read/list, generate-cli with bundling and Bun-compiled binaries, emit-ts in .d.ts or client mode, serve as an MCP bridge, auto-OAuth promotion via `mcporter auth`.
Design detail worth praising in the review: --json produces a stable envelope on stdout while human progress, prompts and warnings always go to stderr so pipes stay parseable.

competitors.name: agent-codemode SECURITY.md (the most quotable document in the repo)
key_points: The package's own contract: it reads credentials, never writes/refreshes/rotates/deletes them, never transmits a token anywhere except to the server that issued it, never caches a token (re-reads the store each call because Claude Code rotates on its own schedule), never prints secret material, and raises loudly on expiry rather than degrading into an empty result.

The disclosure that makes this article: on macOS Claude Code stores every MCP OAuth token in one Keychain item (service 'Claude Code-credentials') that is readable without a prompt by any process running as you that Claude Code could have spawned — including every hook, every local MCP subprocess, every npx package one of those pulls in, and every shell command an agent decides to run.

Consequence stated by the author and worth repeating verbatim in substance: every MCP token you hold, production included, is readable by any process started from a Claude Code session; that is a property of the credential store, not of this package, and removing the package does not change it.

Two practical rules from the doc: treat the agent's MCP server list as a blast radius ('if hyre-prod is one npx away from an untrusted postinstall script, that is worth knowing deliberately rather than discovering later'), and prefer read-scoped tokens where a server offers scopes.

Its own risk scope is genuinely small: no network listener, no daemon, no background process, no persistent state — it runs, reads a credential, makes one JSON-RPC call, exits. The one new capability is convenience, and the doc names the consequence: a script with your Linear token can close tickets at 3am with no one reading the diff, so keep destructive paths behind an explicit flag (the example keeps Slack posting behind --post).

stats.fact: Verified credential sources by platform: macOS reads the Keychain item 'Claude Code-credentials' whose mcpOAuth map is keyed <serverName>|<urlHash> (serverUrl, accessToken, refreshToken, clientId, issuer, expiresAt); Linux/Windows read ~/.claude/.credentials.json for OAuth and always read ~/.claude.json (top-level and per-project mcpServers) plus .mcp.json for stdio/API-key servers, expanding ${VAR} as Claude Code does.

Two documented limits with stated reasons: (1) claude.ai connectors (Gmail, Calendar) are unsupported because their token lives only in claude.ai's backend and the endpoint rejects any clientInfo.name containing 'claude'; (2) Linux/Windows are unverified best-effort — the README asks for help confirming a full run.

Token rotation is a live failure mode: Claude Code refresh tokens are single-use (referencing anthropics/claude-code issue #59460), so a token a script cached or held can be rejected; the documented recovery is to start Claude Code or run `claude mcp login <server>`.

angles: Lead with the number, then immediately right-size it. 262,159 chars vs 903 chars is a real measurement on one task, and the honest read is 'this is the shape of the win, not the size' — cite Agent Swarm's ~99.2% step saving against ~50% end-to-end cost to show what happens when the same trick is measured on a whole job. The article's credibility comes from being the first write-up that refuses to repeat 99.66% without the caveat.

The credential last mile is the actual product. Every other code-mode tool makes you re-authenticate: Cloudflare takes bindings you configure, MCPorter keeps its own vault at ~/.mcporter/credentials.json, VoidMCP wants tokens registered via CLI. agent-codemode's entire differentiated row in its own comparison table is 'your agent's, inherited'. Explain why that decides behaviour — an agent mid-task reaches for what works right now, not for something that needs you to complete an OAuth flow — and then explain what inheriting costs you (next angle).

The security angle is the strongest original contribution this article can make: the package's own SECURITY.md admits that on macOS every MCP OAuth token sits in one Keychain item readable without a prompt by anything a Claude Code session can spawn — hooks, local MCP subprocesses, npx packages, shell commands. So agent-codemode does not create the exposure, it makes an existing one legible. Pair it with the MCP-registry governance data (no auth method recorded, no security review, ~36% of servers untouched for 3+ months) to turn a narrow tool review into a piece about blast radius: authenticate only what you would let any agent-spawned process hold.

Kill the myth that this is new. Code mode was named by Kenton Varda and Sunil Pai at Cloudflare in September 2025; Cloudflare already put 2,500 endpoints behind search()+execute() in ~1,000 tokens; Anthropic ships Programmatic Tool Calling inside the API; MCPorter got to runtime-and-CLI-for-MCP first with 5,039 stars and ~538k weekly downloads. Then show what the honest remainder is: a 33-file, zero-dependency Node CLI whose only novel move is reading a file (or a Keychain item) somebody else already wrote. That is a feature, and a maintenance risk.

The skill is the mechanism, not the library — and the benchmark proves it is fragile. agent-codemode ships .claude/skills/agent-codemode/SKILL.md precisely because 'an agent that doesn't [know] keeps doing what it knows, one tool call at a time'. The independent 160-run benchmark found unguided hybrids guessed nested tool names, misparsed result.content[0].text, made redundant verification calls, and paid 4,328 median initial-context tokens versus 3,261 for direct-only. Behavioural defaulting is the real interface, and it is where this breaks.

Answer 'who is this for' with the task-shape heuristic rather than a call-count threshold: script it when there are 10+ similar calls, a bulk fan-out, heavy intermediate data you would otherwise discard, or a long deterministic chain; keep direct tool calls for a handful of calls, semantic decisions, approvals, errors and rich native results. The 148,000-chars-to-100-chars dataset reduction and the 8-cycles-to-1-cell chain are the two concrete illustrations.

The second win nobody prices: the script is a file. It runs tomorrow from cron or as a CI gate with no model and no tokens — which is the answer to 'isn't code mode on top of MCP on top of code mode a useless layer?'. Agent Swarm's numbers back it (~150 reusable scripts, ~25,000 executions in 30 days, ~70% of schedules using at least one); the counterweight is the author's own warning that a script holding a live Linear token can close tickets at 3am with nobody reading the diff, hence the --post flag pattern.

Review the maintenance reality as a verdict input, not a footnote: no commits since 2026-08-19, no GitHub releases, 30 stars, 0 forks, ~10 weekly npm downloads, one open issue that is a directory invite, and Linux/Windows explicitly unverified. A tool whose whole value is reading a credential store that another vendor controls will rot when that store changes — which Claude Code's single-use refresh rotation (issue #59460) already demonstrates.

Disambiguate the name for search traffic: 'agent codemode' currently returns three unrelated projects — janwilmake's JS package (the subject), datalayer's Python package that generates programmatic tools and can re-serve them over MCP, and Cloudflare's @cloudflare/codemode runtime. A short comparison box earns the keyword and prevents the reader from installing the wrong thing.

Show the five-line core so readers can copy the idea instead of the dependency. The whole trick is: locate the agent's credential store (Keychain mcpOAuth on macOS, ~/.claude/.credentials.json elsewhere), pick the entry for a server, speak Streamable HTTP MCP (initialize -> Mcp-Session-Id -> notifications/initialized -> tools/call) or spawn the stdio subprocess and speak JSON-RPC newline-framed, then print the result. Framing it as a pattern other harnesses can adopt in an afternoon is both accurate and more useful than a verdict on a 30-star repo.
